A.explanation: 0.1 is the linear scale factor of model to full-size, not the stress ratio which depends on volume divided by area.

B.explanation: Stress is not the same because weight falls as $L^3$ while cable area falls as $L^2$, so stress must change with size.

C.explanation: Force scales as $L^3$ and area as $L^2$, so stress scales as $L$, giving a full-size to model ratio of 10.

D.explanation: 100 is the area scale factor $(10^2)$, but stress also includes the $10^3$ scaling of weight, so the ratio is not 100.

hints: Notice the cable tension equals the weight of the cube-shaped load because it is lifted at constant speed, so $F = mg$.
Recall tensile stress is $stress = F/A$ and the load weight is $density \times volume \times g$ with the same material density in model and full-size.
Compare scalings for linear size $L$: cube volume scales as $L^3$ but cable cross-sectional area scales as $L^2$, so work out how $F/A$ scales with $L$.
walkthrough: Identify the force in the cable: at constant speed resultant force is zero, so tension $F$ equals load weight $W = \rho V g$, where $\rho$ is the same for model and full-size.
State the stress rule: $stress = F/A = W/A$, where $A$ is the cross-sectional area of the cable.
Scale the weight: linear dimensions are $1/10$, so volume $V$ scales as $length^3$. Hence $V_{full}/V_{model} = 10^3 = 1000$, so $W_{full}/W_{model} = 1000$.
Scale the area: cable diameter also scales with $L$, so area $A$ scales as $length^2$. Hence $A_{full}/A_{model} = 10^2 = 100$.
